findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet will raise ValueError/AssertionError
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` directly. Django's QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative start/stop indices (raises `ValueError`/`AssertionError`, 'Negative indexing is not supported.'). The surrounding comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically,' which is incorrect. Any authorized caller (superuser or org member with global access) who sets `optimized_pagination=true` and supplies a cursor with a negative offset will get an unhandled exception/500 error instead of a page of results.

findings.title: Behavior change in shared BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets for all paginator subclasses
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` was made directly in `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is the shared base class used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and other paginators across the entire codebase — not just the new audit-log-specific `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. Previously a negative offset (e.g. from a malformed/tampered cursor string) would raise an error from the underlying queryset slice. Now, for non-prev cursors, a negative offset is silently clamped to 0, changing the result set returned (restarting from the first page) instead of surfacing an error. This is a behavior change affecting every endpoint that uses these paginators, introduced to support a single endpoint's opt-in feature, and risks unintended regressions elsewhere. The `is_prev` branch is left unclamped and will still raise on negative offsets, so the fix is also inconsistent.

findings.title: Potential AttributeError if organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without checking that `member` is not None. If `request.user.is_superuser` is False and `organization_context.member` is None (e.g. a staff/non-member user who is nonetheless authorized by `OrganizationAuditPermission`), this will raise an `AttributeError` and return a 500 instead of a handled 403/empty result. Elsewhere in the codebase this pattern is typically guarded as `organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access`.

findings.title: No tests added for new optimized pagination branch or permission gating
findings.body: This PR introduces a new conditional code path (`optimized_pagination=true` query param combined with superuser/global-access gating, routed to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`) but does not add or update any tests for the endpoint. Given this path has a concrete bug (negative offset slicing crashes, see paginator.py), and changes authorization-sensitive behavior, the lack of test coverage is a significant gap that would have caught the crash before merge.

findings.title: New OptimizedCursorPaginator class has no unit tests
findings.body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class (101 lines of new pagination logic, including the negative-offset code path) has no accompanying unit tests in the diff. Core pagination logic like this is exactly the kind of code that needs direct test coverage for boundary conditions (empty cursor, prev cursor, negative offset, hits counting), none of which are exercised here.

findings.title: Misleading comment about negative offset support
findings.body: The added comment states this enables 'efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets' via negative offsets, but `Cursor` itself does nothing to validate or support negative offsets safely — the actual slicing logic in `paginator.py` that consumes `cursor.offset` will raise an error when given a negative value (Django disallows negative slice bounds). The comment implies functionality that does not actually work end-to-end.
